title: Gwinnett couple warn others after losing $800K in cryptocurrency scam

reading.body:
A cryptocurrency scam defrauded a Georgia couple of nearly $800,000 by deploying a fake website with AI-generated content. The fraudsters used a WhatsApp message to initiate contact, then directed the victim to a real trading app where they displayed false account balances on his screen using the fabricated website. The deception worked by allowing small successful withdrawals initially, establishing enough trust to encourage larger investments before the money disappeared.

The failure was in the lack of authentication between what the victim saw on screen and what actually existed in his account. The real trading app was legitimate, but criminals intercepted the display layer to show false information. A system design that required independent verification of balances through channels the user controlled, or that prevented screen manipulation of financial data, would have exposed the fraud before the largest withdrawals were attempted.

It is not established whether the app's creators knew their platform was being exploited this way, or what technical vulnerabilities enabled the screen manipulation.

reports.title: Georgia couple loses $800K in sophisticated cryptocurrency scam
Gwinnett couple warn others after losing $800K in cryptocurrency scam

summary:
A retired Georgia couple lost nearly $800,000 in a cryptocurrency scam that started with a WhatsApp message from a stranger. The scammer convinced Jerry Dunaway to invest through a mobile trading app, initially allowing small withdrawals to build trust before gradually increasing investment amounts. The app appeared legitimate, but scammers had created an AI-generated fake website that showed false account balances on Jerry's screen. When he tried to withdraw a larger sum last week, he discovered the money was gone and contacted police.

The couple, Jerry and Mindy Dunaway, are now speaking publicly to warn others about the sophisticated tactics used by scammers. Police confirmed the trading app itself was real, but criminals manipulated what appeared on the screen. Investigators indicated that victims in similar cases rarely recover their stolen funds. The Dunaways' children have created a GoFundMe campaign to help their parents with daily expenses as they work with Gwinnett County police on the case.
